title: Scale a Prototype from 100 to 100,000 Users
subtitle: Turn a hundred-user assistant into an operated, evaluated service for a hundred thousand employees.
author: By Sourav Banerjee

practice_prompts.label: What "works" meant and what the pilot hid
practice_prompts.hint: Ask the discovery questions, then name the four things demos hide and the three extra gaps.

practice_prompts.label: Users to requests, tokens and dollars
practice_prompts.hint: Rebuild 240,000/day, 20/s, 7.8M tokens/min, 100 in flight and the $122,000 to $67,000 cost ladder.

practice_prompts.label: Tenfold steps, gateway and three boundaries
practice_prompts.hint: Say what breaks at each step, then trace one request through admission, isolation and change control.

practice_prompts.label: Failover, eval, rollout, owners and adoption
practice_prompts.hint: Retry inside a breaker with a warm fallback; slice-gated eval; user cohorts with a pointer flip; owners; week-4 retention.

practice_prompts.label: The Finance cost pivot
practice_prompts.hint: Driver, cheapest lever, proving metric, what not to do, and the 60-second line.

rubric: Challenged what "works" meant and said which pilot evidence does not transfer before sizing anything.
Sized from licensed users to requests a second, tokens a minute and dollars a month, and said adoption is a cost variable (about 300x, not 1,000x).
Named what breaks at each tenfold step in order: identity, then capacity, then fairness and organisation.
Put one gateway in front of every call and separated the rate limit (whether) from the fair queue (in what order), with budgets checked before the call.
Kept permission scope in retrieval and every cache key, with the security slice gated at zero.
Chained retry inside a breaker with a warm, separately evaluated fallback, and refused to promise more uptime than the provider gives.
Rolled out by user cohort through shadow and canary with a tested pointer-flip rollback.
Named owners, runbooks and a support ladder, and measured adoption with week-4 retention and override rate.
Answered the cost pivot with routing, prefix caching, output caps, batching and pre-call budgets, proved by cost per successful task.

editorial_review.evidence: Re-review against all 27 captured sections, item by item, producing 69 coverage rows. The previous version was a thin paraphrase: it dropped the source-contribution table, the prompt and bank quotes, the weak/strong answer, admit-assemble-answer-learn, the two-minute spoken answer, the seven carrying lines, the four cost verbs, the runbook and adoption quotes, all nine adoption causes verbatim, and the cost-pivot framing. It also mis-captioned the tenfold figure, left the three architecture figures as 'source figure 1/2/3', showed ', ' where the sizing table had a dash, and had blank cost-card headers and broken abbr text. Restored all of these, added two walkthrough steps (eval rebuild, adoption) so section 9 and 12 are no longer split across deep dives, made the six follow-ups, the cost pivot and the two-minute answer into reveals, and rewrote the Quick review to cover all fifteen takeaways. Rechecked every sizing and cost product and resolved three source issues. The brief opens on the volunteer-to-employee gap, defines tail latency, token, tenant, gateway, 429 and cohort, and skips a separate example because step 6 traces one request. Source inconsistencies resolved in text (2026-11-16): caching row assumed every mid-tier request hits and ignored the write charge → write cost added (1.25x input, five-minute lifetime, a shared prefix stays warm, at most 288 writes a day, under $1.10), net saving about $193 a day so the $2,460/$74,000 row stands; component and owner tables had no adoption entry → Adoption row added to both (cohort waves, champions and metrics; product owner with the executive sponsor and champions), from the source's own rollout and change-management material; override-rate metric worded for agents while this assistant has read-only tools → defined as a reviewer editing, rejecting or correcting an answer before use, with the source's reading paraphrased for the assistant.
